key_concepts: Living things grow, respond, and reproduce.
Nonliving things do not grow, move, or need food.
Examples of living things include plants, animals, and people.
Examples of nonliving things include rocks, chairs, and tables.

Animals respond to their surroundings, such as reacting to sounds to stay safe.
Plants also respond to their surroundings, including light, gravity, and touch.
Reproduction means living things make more of their own kind.
Animals reproduce by giving birth or laying eggs.
Offspring resemble their parents, such as kittens looking like cats.
Living things cannot come from nonliving things.
